title: Sex chromosome aneuploidy — XXY
clinical_history: A 19-year-old man is evaluated for tall stature, gynecomastia, and small testes. Semen analysis shows azoospermia. Constitutional karyotyping is requested.
plain_language_interpretation: A male karyotype with 47 chromosomes due to an extra X chromosome (sex-chromosome complement XXY).
explanation: The extra chromosome is a second X, producing XXY and a count of 47. ISCN writes this as 47,XXY rather than 46,XY,+X. Klinefelter syndrome is the corresponding clinical diagnosis in a phenotypic male: hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, infertility, and often tall stature. Distinguish this from 47,XYY, which has two Y chromosomes and a different phenotype.
hints: The count is 47. Identify whether the extra chromosome is an autosome or a sex chromosome.
There are two X chromosomes and one Y. Place both X chromosomes in group C and the Y in group G.
Sex-chromosome complements such as XXY are written in the second ISCN field (47,XXY), not as 46,XY,+X.
